traditions/church-of-north-india/summary: Inaugurated at Nagpur in 1970 by six churches, including — unusually — Baptists, Brethren and Disciples alongside Anglicans, Methodists, Presbyterians and Congregationalists. It accepted both infant and believers' baptism and the historic episcopate. It is a member of the Anglican Communion, the World Methodist Council and the World Communion of Reformed Churches.
traditions/church-of-north-india/profile: Salvation by grace through faith in Christ.
Baptism (infant or believer) and the Lord's Supper; confirmation.
Episcopal-synodical: Synod, Moderator and diocesan bishops.
Liturgical and free worship in Hindi and many languages.
traditions/united-church-of-canada/summa: Formed in 1925 by Canadian Methodists, Congregationalists, most Presbyterians and western local union churches. Long Canada's largest Protestant church, it has been a progressive voice: it ordained Lydia Gruchy (1936), approved the ordination of gay and lesbian people (1988) and apologised for its role in the Indian residential schools. Its membership has declined sharply since the 1960s.
traditions/united-church-of-canada/disti: Progressive positions on sexuality and justice
traditions/united-church-of-canada/profi: Scripture as primary source, with the Basis of Union and later statements (A Song of Faith, 2006).
Grace of God in Christ for all; personal and social transformation.
Hope for God's reign of justice and peace.
Presbyterian-conciliar: congregations, regional councils and a General Council with a Moderator.
Reformed and Methodist worship traditions; Voices United hymnal.
traditions/uniting-church-in-australia/s: Formed in 1977 by Methodists, most Presbyterians and most Congregationalists on the theologically substantial Basis of Union (1971). It is the third-largest denomination in Australia and a major provider of community services (UnitingCare). It entered a covenant with its Aboriginal and Islander members (1994) and affirmed the First Peoples in its constitution's Preamble (2009). In 2018 it allowed ministers to conduct same-sex marriages.
traditions/uniting-church-in-australia/d: Basis of Union as founding theological charter
Covenant with Uniting Aboriginal and Islander Christian Congress
Ordination of women from the start
traditions/uniting-church-in-australia/p: Scripture as unique prophetic and apostolic testimony, with the ecumenical creeds and Reformation witnesses named in the Basis of Union.
Salvation by grace through faith in Christ.
Baptism (infants and believers) and the Lord's Supper.
The church as a pilgrim people moving toward a promised goal.
Inter-conciliar: congregation, presbytery, synod and assembly.
Reformed and Methodist worship; Uniting in Worship.
traditions/uniting-church-in-australia/s: Active; c. 673,000 people identified with it in the 2021 census.
traditions/united-church-of-christ/summa: Formed in 1957 by the Evangelical and Reformed Church (German Reformed and Lutheran-Reformed 'Evangelical' roots) and the Congregational Christian Churches (New England Puritan heritage). Theologically liberal and congregational in polity, it ordained the first openly gay minister in a mainline church (William R. Johnson, 1972), and endorsed same-sex marriage (2005). Its motto: 'That they may all be one' (John 17:21).
traditions/united-church-of-christ/disti: Union of Congregational and German Reformed/Evangelical streams
Statement of Faith (1959) as testimony, not test
traditions/united-church-of-christ/profi: Scripture and the historic creeds as testimonies; freedom of conscience.
Grace of God in Christ for all.
Hope for the realm of God.
Congregational covenant with associations, conferences and General Synod.
Diverse Reformed worship; New Century Hymnal.
traditions/kyodan/name: United Church of Christ in Japan (Nihon Kirisuto Kyodan)
traditions/kyodan/summary: Japan's largest Protestant church, formed in 1941 when the government required Protestant denominations to unite under the Religious Organizations Law. After 1945 several groups withdrew, but the Kyodan continued as a united church of mainly Presbyterian, Methodist and Congregational heritage. Its 1967 Confession on Responsibility during the Second World War acknowledged its wartime complicity; Kyodan members in Okinawa have played a prominent role in peace activism.
traditions/kyodan/distinctives/0: United Protestant church in a minority setting
traditions/kyodan/distinctives/4: Theological debate over the church and the emperor system
traditions/kyodan/profile/authority: Scripture with the Apostles' Creed and the Kyodan Confession of Faith (1954).
traditions/kyodan/profile/salvation: Salvation by grace through faith in Christ.
traditions/kyodan/profile/worship: Reformed and Methodist forms of worship.
traditions/kyodan/status: Active; small in absolute terms but central to Japanese Protestantism.
traditions/ecumenical-patriarchate/summa: The see of Constantinople (Istanbul), whose bishop was ranked second after Rome by the Council of Constantinople (381) and given wide jurisdiction by canon 28 of Chalcedon (451). Since 1054 it has been regarded by the Orthodox as 'first among equals' among autocephalous churches. Its direct flock in Turkey is small, but it oversees Mount Athos, Crete and the Dodecanese, the autonomous churches of Finland and Estonia and many diaspora dioceses, including the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America.
traditions/ecumenical-patriarchate/disti: Primacy of honour ('first among equals') among Orthodox churches
Claimed right to grant autocephaly and hear appeals (contested by Moscow)
Spiritual centre at the Phanar in Istanbul
Jurisdiction over much of the diaspora under canon 28 of Chalcedon
Leading role in ecumenism and environmental theology ('the Green Patriarch')
traditions/ecumenical-patriarchate/profi: Holy Tradition, of which Scripture is the summit, interpreted through the seven ecumenical councils, the Fathers and the liturgy; the conciliar mind of the bishops in communion. The Patriarch convenes and coordinates, but does not rule other churches.
Salvation is theosis: union with God by grace through Christ in the Holy Spirit, received in baptism and lived out in faith, repentance, prayer and the sacramental life of the Church.
Seven principal Mysteries (baptism by triple immersion, chrismation, Eucharist, confession, ordination, marriage, holy unction), with infant communion; leavened bread in the Eucharist.
Expectation of Christ's return, the resurrection and judgement; prayer for the departed and the communion of saints; no doctrine of purgatory.
Patriarch with the Holy and Sacred Synod; metropolitans in Turkey, semi-autonomous churches (Crete) and eparchies abroad. Patriarch Bartholomew I since 1991.
Byzantine rite in Greek (and local languages abroad), Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom, Byzantine chant, Revised Julian calendar for fixed feasts.
Old Testament from the Septuagint, including the books Protestants call deuterocanonical (anagignoskomena), and the 27-book New Testament.
traditions/ecumenical-patriarchate/statu: Active. The Halki theological school has been closed by Turkish law since 1971. Relations with Moscow were broken after Constantinople's 2018–19 Ukrainian decision.
traditions/church-of-greece/summary: The autocephalous Orthodox church of the Greek state, declared independent of Constantinople in 1833 and recognised by the Ecumenical Patriarchate's Tomos of 1850. The Greek constitution names Eastern Orthodoxy the 'prevailing religion'. Metropolises of the 'New Lands' annexed after 1912 are administered by the Church of Greece while remaining canonically under Constantinople; Crete and the Dodecanese stay with the Patriarchate.
traditions/church-of-greece/distinctives: National church closely tied to Greek identity and state
Holy Synod presided over by the Archbishop of Athens
Recognised the Orthodox Church of Ukraine in 2019
Mount Athos remains under Constantinople, not Athens
traditions/church-of-greece/profile/auth: Holy Tradition, of which Scripture is the summit, interpreted through the seven ecumenical councils, the Fathers and the liturgy; the conciliar mind of the bishops in communion.
traditions/church-of-greece/profile/salv: Salvation is theosis: union with God by grace through Christ in the Holy Spirit, received in baptism and lived out in faith, repentance, prayer and the sacramental life of the Church.
traditions/church-of-greece/profile/sacr: Seven principal Mysteries (baptism by triple immersion, chrismation, Eucharist, confession, ordination, marriage, holy unction), with infant communion; leavened bread in the Eucharist.
traditions/church-of-greece/profile/esch: Expectation of Christ's return, the resurrection and judgement; prayer for the departed and the communion of saints; no doctrine of purgatory.
traditions/church-of-greece/profile/gove: Archbishop of Athens and All Greece with the Holy Synod and the Synod of the Hierarchy of all metropolitans; clergy salaries historically paid by the state.
traditions/church-of-greece/profile/wors: Byzantine rite in Koine Greek with Byzantine chant; Revised Julian calendar (adopted 1924), with Old Calendarist minorities who reject it.
traditions/church-of-greece/profile/cano: Old Testament from the Septuagint, including the books Protestants call deuterocanonical (anagignoskomena), and the 27-book New Testament.
traditions/church-of-greece/status: Active; the large majority of Greeks are baptised Orthodox. Old Calendarist groups (from 1924) are outside its communion.
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/name: Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch and All the East
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/summary: The Chalcedonian (Byzantine-rite) Patriarchate of Antioch, claiming foundation by the apostles Peter and Paul, whose seat has been in Damascus since the fourteenth century. After the separation of the non-Chalcedonian Syriac Orthodox line (6th century), it became the church of the Arabic-speaking 'Rum' Orthodox of Syria and Lebanon. Since 1899 its patriarchs have been Arabs. A large emigrant church exists in the Americas and Australia.
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/distincti: Seat in Damascus; Balamand as theological centre
Antiochian Orthodox Archdiocese of North America, with a Western Rite vicariate
Strong presence in Latin America through Levantine emigration
Suffering and displacement in the Syrian war (from 2011)
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/profile/a: Holy Tradition, of which Scripture is the summit, interpreted through the seven ecumenical councils, the Fathers and the liturgy; the conciliar mind of the bishops in communion.
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/profile/s: Salvation is theosis: union with God by grace through Christ in the Holy Spirit, received in baptism and lived out in faith, repentance, prayer and the sacramental life of the Church.
Seven principal Mysteries (baptism by triple immersion, chrismation, Eucharist, confession, ordination, marriage, holy unction), with infant communion; leavened bread in the Eucharist.
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/profile/e: Expectation of Christ's return, the resurrection and judgement; prayer for the departed and the communion of saints; no doctrine of purgatory.
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/profile/g: Patriarch (John X since 2012) with the Holy Synod of metropolitans; self-ruling archdioceses abroad.
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/profile/w: Byzantine liturgy in Arabic, Greek and English; Byzantine chant with Arabic adaptation; Revised Julian calendar except for Pascha.
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/profile/c: Old Testament from the Septuagint, including the books Protestants call deuterocanonical (anagignoskomena), and the 27-book New Testament.
traditions/antiochian-orthodox/status: Active; it broke communion with the Patriarchate of Jerusalem in 2014 over Jerusalem's creation of a see in Qatar, which Antioch regards as its territory.
